title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.57): S is a base with residue characteristics ≠ 2. The page establishes the equivalence of three kinds of data.

(i) A pair (E,σ), where E/S is proper and smooth with geometrically connected fibres of dimension 1 and genus 1, and σ is an involution inducing −id on Pic^0_{E/S} = E_0.

(ii) A section a of Pic^2_{E/S} ≅ E ∧_{E_0} E. Given a, set σ(x) = a − x, i.e. x + σx ~ a. Conversely, the class x + σ(x) is constant and defines a.

(iii) A pair (E_0, I), where E_0 is an elliptic curve over S and I is a torsor under V := E_0[2]. Starting from (E,σ), one takes I = E^σ = {x : 2x = a}.

The passage from (iii) to (i) is formula (21): E = I ∧^V E_0, the push-out of the V-torsor I along V ⊂ E_0. The involution σ is induced by x ↦ −x on E_0, which is legitimate because −1 is trivial on V.

V = E_0[2] acts on E by translation, commuting with σ (the NB in the margin). There is an isomorphism (22) E/V ≅ E_0, explicitly x ↦ 2x − a, using E ∧_{E_0} E ≅ Pic^2. It intertwines σ with σ_0 = −1. In modern terms, E → E_0 is the 2-covering attached to the class of I in H^1(S, E_0[2]), i.e. a twist of [2]: E_0 → E_0.

Next he forms the quotients (23): X = E/{1,σ} and Σ = E_0/{1,σ_0}. These are P^1-bundles (Severi–Brauer schemes of relative dimension 1, i.e. conic bundles). V acts on X and (24) X/V ≅ Σ. The ramification divisor of (25) E → X is I, the 4-point fixed locus.

On the next page, I → X is a V-equivariant monomorphism into the locus X* where V acts freely. This puts the data into the framework of §2: Σ ≅ Σ_J with J = V^* (Cartier dual, ≅ V via the Weil pairing), and I is the inverse image of a section of Σ_J minus D_J.

Purpose: a torsor-theoretic, base-independent description of genus-1 curves with a degree-2 class (equivalently, double covers of a conic branched in a V-torsor of 4 points). This serves a modular description of elliptic curves over Z[1/2] through P^1-bundles with an action of a Klein-four-type group scheme.
errors: No mathematical errors found. Calling X a 'fibré en droites projectives' should be read as a Severi–Brauer conic bundle (not necessarily the projectivization of a rank-2 vector bundle), which is presumably what is meant.
Minor: the statement that the data (E,σ) and the data (E,a) are equivalent implicitly uses E ≅ Pic^1_{E/S}, i.e. that E is a torsor under E_0. This is fine because the curve is smooth of genus 1.

ideas.what: An involution of a genus-1 curve acting as −1 on the Jacobian is equivalent to a section of Pic^2 (σ(x) = a − x)
ideas.modern_name: hyperelliptic involution attached to a degree-2 linear system / genus-one double cover of a conic

ideas.what: E = I ∧^{E_0[2]} E_0 with E → E_0, x ↦ 2x − a, i.e. E/V ≅ E_0
ideas.modern_name: 2-coverings of an elliptic curve classified by H^1(S, E_0[2]) (2-descent, twist of multiplication by 2)

ideas.what: Quotients X = E/σ, Σ = E_0/(−1) as P^1-bundles with E_0[2] acting, X/V ≅ Σ, ramification locus = the V-torsor I
ideas.modern_name: Kummer line / Klein four-group action on P^1 and branch points (Legendre form, level-2 structure)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Klein; Legendre form); relative versions in moduli literature

deep.surprise_reason: A clean relative, torsor-theoretic formulation of classical facts: genus-one double covers of conics, 2-coverings classified by E[2]-torsors, and Klein-four actions on P^1. It is careful but standard. Its value lies in its role in Grothendieck's larger construction (the Σ_J of §2), not in anything new on this page.
transcription_corrections: The isolated '21' below '(22)' and above 'E∧_{E_0}E ≃ Pic^2_{E/S}' looks like a cross-reference or reminder rather than an equation label. The displayed isomorphism is the one used to define the map E/V → E_0.

First lines: '... induisant −id sur Pic^0_{E/S}, équivaut à une section de Pic^2_{E/S} (≃ E∧_{E_0}E), ou encore à celles de (E_0, I), où E_0 est une courbe elliptique relative sur S et où I est un torseur sous V =def ₂(E_0)'.
(21), second line: 'σ déduit de la symétrie x ↦ −x de E_0 via la formule précédente'.
